claims.note: Added a vision subsection connecting final outputs to inheritable knowledge.
Explained that conventional documents preserve conclusions while losing the checkable path that formed them.
Distinguished accepted external reasoning records from private verbatim chain of thought.
Defined the deeper AI-slop problem as output without stable provenance that cannot be safely inherited or accumulated.
Set out the progression from artifact ledger to shared protocol to collective-intelligence accumulation unit.
Introduced the Git analogy as trusted collaboration expanding from code to knowledge.
Added the positioning line that Git made code collaborative and Proofpress makes intelligence cumulative.
Added the positioning line contrasting code history with knowledge provenance.
Framed Proofpress as a protocol for three foundational human-machine knowledge questions rather than another docs product.
Added the three questions covering knowledge, trust, and continuation.
Closed the prose vision around memory, lineage, trust, and inheritable collective intelligence.

context.why: Richard supplied an earlier vision discussion that captured why Proofpress matters beyond provenance tooling; the canonical strategy now preserves that argument as polished prose connecting artifact history, AI slop, Git-like trusted collaboration, and cumulative human-agent collective intelligence.
